violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program
violations.observation: A CFM WAS NOT PRESENT AT THE BEGINNING OF INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: Obtain a certified food managers certificate from an accredited program. CFM CAME TO FACILITY SHORTLY AFTER INSPECTION STARTED.

violations.title: Where to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee was observed cleaning their hands in a food preparation sink, warewashing sink or in a mop sink. EHS OBSERVED PIC WASH THEIR HANDS AT A PREP SINK USED TO RINSE DISHES OFF BEFORE THEY ARE PLACED IN THE DISH WASHER.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands in ONLY a designated handsink. PLEASE MAKE SURE TO ONLY BE WASHING HANDS AT DESIGNATED HAND SINKS. Pho Golden Cow 2 (Inspection Date: 06/02/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: OBSERVED HAND THE LEFT OF THE 3 VAT SINK, BEING USED TO STORE A KNIFE, FORK AND TO GO CONTAINER.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. PIC REMOVED THE ITEMS FROM THE HAND SINK AT TIME OF INSPECTION.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR, RAW SHELL EGGS WERE BEING STORED ABOVE READY TO EAT SAUCES. IN THE 2DR PREP TOP(2), RAW BEEF WAS BEING STORED ON TOP OF RTE COOKED BEEF.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. PLEASE REMEMBER ALL RAW FOODS NEED TO BE STORED BELOW RTE FOODS TO PREVENT THE POTENTIAL OF BACTERIA GROWTH AND SPREAD. PIC MOVED ALL RAW FOODS BEFORE RTE FOODS IN BOTH THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR AND THE 2DR PREP TOP (2).

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: bean sprouts being stored on prep table near dish in an ice bath machine, were temping at 59F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC THREW AWAY BEAN SPROUTS DUE TO NOT KNOWING HOW LONG BEAN SPROUTS WERE OUT OF TEMPERATURE. PIC REPLACED BEAN SPROUTS AND ALSO REPLACED THE WATER AND ICE IN THE ICE BATH TO HELP KEEP THE TEMPERATURE DOWN FOR THE NEW BEAN SPROUTS. PIC WILL CHECK TEMPERATURE OF BEAN SPROUTS EVER HOUR TO MAKE SURE THEY ARE STAYING AT 41F OR BELOW.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: Multiple squeeze bottles and seasoning shakers inside of the kitchen did not have a proper label.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. PLEASE REMEMBER TO LABEL ALL FOOD ITEMS THAT ARE TAKEN OUT OF ITS ORIGINAL CONTAINER AND PLACED INTO A DIFFERENT ONE. PLEASE LABEL ALL SQUEEZE BOTTLES AND SEASONING CONTAINERS BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION, IN 6 MONTHS.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. MULTIPLE CONTAINERS OF BROTH AND DIFFERENT SAUCES WHERE BEING STORED IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR ON THE FLOOR.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL FOODS MUST BE AT LEAST 6 INHCES OFF THE GROUND AT ALL TIMES. PIC WILL WORK WITH EMPLOYEES TO HAVE FOOD PROPERLY STORED OFF THR GROUND BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION, IN 6 MONTHS.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: RICE PADDLES WITH HANDLES WERE BEING STORED IN WATER NEXT TO COUNTER TOP RICE WARMER, THAT WAS ONLY TEMPING AT 77F.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PLEASE REMEMBER ALL IN USE UTENSILS MUST BE STORED IN WATER THAT IS AT LEAST 135F OR HIGHER. THIS IS TO HELP THE POTENTIAL BACTER GROWRH ON THE UTENSILS. PIC EMPTIED THE CONTAINER OF WATER HOLDING THE UTENSILS AND PUT THEM TO BE WASHED, RINSED AND SANITIZED. PIC ALSO REPLACED THE RICE PADDLE WITH A NEW ONE.

violations.title: Chemical Sanitization, Chlorine Requirements
violations.observation: When tested, the low temperature, chemical sanitizing warewashing machine was observed with a sanitizing rinse concentration of less than 50 ppm chlorine solution.
violations.corrective_action: Immediately discontinue use of the dishmachine. Until the machine is adequately repaired, set up the three-compartment sink to manually wash, rinse and sanitize food-contact surfaces using a sanitizing solution at the proper concentration of at least 50 to 200 ppm total chlorine. THE SANITIZER IN THE DISH MACHINE WAS NOT DISPENSING INTO THE DISH WASHER AT TIME OF INSPECTION. PIC WAS ABLE TO PROPERLY FLUSH THE TUBE USED TO PULL IN THE SANITIZER SOLUTION INTO THE DISH MACHINE. AFTER RUNNING THE MACHINE AN ADDITIONAL TWO TIMES, THE CONCENTRATION OF THE SANITIZER SOLUTION WAS IN THE CORRECT RANGE.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Poison/Toxic Material, Conditions of Use
violations.observation: Pesticides labeled for residential use were observed in the facility and are being applied by the operator to control pests.
violations.corrective_action: Remove residential use pesticides from the facility. When necessary for pest control, chemical pesticides must be applied by a certified pesticide applicator to prevent injury and contamination. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT HOME USE PESTICIDES ARE NOT TO BE USED IN THE FACILITY FOR PEST CONTROL. EHS LOOKED AT LAST INVOICE FOR WHEN PEST CONTROL HAD BEEN COMPLETED LAST AND IT WAS MONTHS PRIOR. PIC CALLED THE PEST CONTROL COMPANY THEY USE AND WAS ABLE TO MAKE AN APPOINTMENT FOR PEST CONTROL APPLICATION TO OCCUR THE FOLLOWING DAY AND WAS ABLE TO SET UP A SCHEDULE FOR THEM TO COME EVERY 2 WEEKS UNTIL THE PEST CONTROL COMPANY DEEMS ITS OKAY TO ONLY GET PEST CONTROL ONCE A MONTH LIKE FACILITY WAS PREVIOUSLY DOING.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: cardboard was being used to line a shelving unit that is used to put food on while cooling from cook temp to 135F, when the cooling process begins and then the food is moved to the walk-in refrigerator. The cardboard was dirty to sight and touch.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. PIC REMOVED AND THREW AWAY THE CARDBOARD. THE EHS DISCUSSED WITH THE PIC OTHER MATERIALS THAT COULD BE USED IN PLACE OF THE CARDBOARD.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Access to Handwashing Sink
violations.observation: The handwashing facility located to the left of the 3 vat sink is blocked by thawing meat in plastic preventing access by employees for easy handwashing
violations.corrective_action: A hand washing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT ALL HAND SINKS MUST BE CLEAR OF ALL DEBRIS INCLUDING THAWING MEAT. HAND SINKS MUST BE AVAILABLE FOR ALL EMPLOYEES TO WASH HANDS TO PREVENT POTENTIAL CONTAMINATION. PIC REMOVED THE MEAT FROM THE SINK.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: bean sprouts sitting on the counter were at 60F during the inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT ALL COLD FOOD MUST BE COLD HELD AT 41F OR BELOW. PIC MOVED THE BEANSPROUTS TO THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR TO COOL DOWN.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: raw beef was thawing in the 3 vat sink at ambient temperature.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. PIC NOW UNDERSTANDS THE CORRECT WAYS TO THAW FOOD PROPERLY. PIC BEGAN TO RUN WATER IN THE 3 VAT SINK AT 70F TO FINSIH THAWING THE BEEF.
